about: A pointer, not a registry: BoltBeam holds no engine patch and no engine kernel artifact. Engine mods (patches and kernels) live in the arkey_ie_mods repo; every mod fact (switch, check, output label, marker, lines, budget, archive) is that repo's index.json: at mods_repo.pin shipped as data/ie_mods_index.json, at a newer commit read by workflow/mods.py when `mods` resolves one; read by workflow/mods.py only. This file keeps BoltBeam-side facts: where the repo is (read only for a patch's text when applying), the pin, which BoltBeam features use which mod (uses, by engine/name), how a kernel gets into an engine (install_paths), how mods are applied per engine (apply), BoltBeam's own patches (own_patches) and the evidence records that are patch files (evidence_patches). sz.py fails on any other tracked or untracked *.patch or *.diff file in the repo.

mods_repo.pin_why: the floor and the offline default, not the only choice: `boltbeam mods` reads the newest commit on the repo's default branch past the pin whose index schema BoltBeam reads and whose requires.boltbeam it meets (workflow/mods.resolve), the pin when that fails; --pin or $BOLTBEAM_IE_MODS_PIN reads exactly one commit
mods_repo.url_why: where `boltbeam mods` clones the repo from (into ~/.boltbeam/arkey_ie_mods, workflow/mods.ensure) when no local clone is configured; a configured clone is used as it is

benchmarks_why: where a mods version's published benchmark (speed and the quality gate) is in arkey_ie_mods, keyed engine/version; `boltbeam mods` names it beside each quality-gated mod it takes (workflow/mods.evidence). A path in the repo's master, not at the pin: the benchmark came after the pinned index
uses_why: by engine/name (the mod in any version); every mod with a switch is also read by results.engine_mods, context_audit.output_label and tune.output_of

plan_only.llama.cpp/rs-one-copy: costs +0.12 ms a decode step [0.04, 0.19] (session-ab, switch on vs off); it pays only when the plan spends the memory it frees (the expert residency placement with the hot draft), so a run on a modded build leaves it off and tune's spend fit names it (LLAMA_RS_ONE_COPY=1) when its plan uses the freed MiB
plan_only.llama.cpp/kv-stream: costs -8.6 tok/s warm decode [-17.8, +0.6] at 128k where everything fits without it (session-ab, 3 pairs, N 65,536 vs off); it pays only where the memory it frees buys expert residency (256k: 220.0 vs 184.4 tok/s), so a run on a modded build leaves it off and tune's spend fit names it (LLAMA_KV_STREAM=N) when its plan uses the freed MiB
plan_only.llama.cpp/rbudget-backend: keeps -bs on under a thinking budget; its gain (+13.8 tok/s warm decode at 256k, replies identical) was measured on one chip and model shape only, so a run on a modded build leaves it off and tune's LLAMA_RBUDGET_BACKEND row sets it where that measurement holds (with -bs under the cap) and states it elsewhere
plan_only.llama.cpp/graph-cpy-kernel: lets CUDA graphs update in place (rebuilds 0.280 -> 0.012 a decode step at 256k, replies identical) but no speed gain has resolved (+0.3 tok/s [-2.8, +3.5], 3 pairs), so a run on a modded build leaves it off and tune's GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_CPY_KERNEL row states it with its evidence
plan_only.llama.cpp/1.0.0/sparse-split: 1.0.0 is frozen: its sm_120 evidence row (sparse-chain-20261119, measured) lets the build carry the mod, but a run on a 1.0.0 modded build leaves its switch off as it was before the pin moved to 617b227; b12521's sparse-split is unaffected (this key names the 1.0.0 mod only)

plan_only_why: mods whose switch a run on a modded build does not turn on by itself (workflow/mods.run_env): tune names it where it pays, its spend fit when its plan pays for the memory it frees, or the mod's own row where its gain was measured (engine/name, as uses, for the mod in every version; engine/version/name for one version's mod)

install_paths.why: How a kernel the search finds gets into an engine's decode, per engine (the kernel ledger's install_path column reads this; an engine with no row has none). status proven: a run showed an outside kernel launched in place of the engine's own at no measured cost; the evidence names it. mod: the arkey_ie_mods mod (by name) whose switch turns it on; a run with it on reads untested until arkey_ie_mods has kernel rows a manifest entry maps to (context_audit.output_label).

commit_match.why: the hook's rule (09 ext_load, ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ext-kernels.cpp:155-168): the build's ggml commit cut at its first suffix_sep (a -dirty marker), never a manifest entry, then equal to one of the manifest's engine.builds on their common prefix of min_prefix or more characters

llama.cpp.loaded_why: the hook takes a manifest only on a build whose commit matches one of its engine.builds (commit_match), then writes this WARN line per entry it loads; llama-server drops ggml INFO lines (common/log.cpp:551/563), so a load is confirmed only by this line
llama.cpp.evidence: boltbeam-runs/ext-kernel-hook-20261115: an identity cubin through the hook on X16 at 128k: 71,425 checks past 98.6k bit-identical, 59/59 replies identical, session step +0.069 ms against 0.158 ms off-vs-off, PDL and graph capture kept

apply.why: screen mods per engine: the applier its mods use and where a build's source checkout is in its folder; an engine with no row lists nothing (vLLM: patch_p1 into a venv copy is not wired yet); where each mod applies is its chip row (data/mod_shapes.json chip_status, else the index row's own chips), not a backend list here

llama.cpp.copy_skip_why: a tree without .git is copied whole: its top-level build directories are not source
llama.cpp.commit_cmake_why: every mods build is configured with the base commit: in a tree without .git ggml says "unknown" and the ext-kernels hook refuses every manifest (09 ext_load: "this build (unknown) is not one the manifest was checked on"), silently running stock kernels. GGML_BUILD_COMMIT alone is not enough: the top-level CMakeLists.txt:158-160 and :224 set it from LLAMA_BUILD_COMMIT, and ggml/CMakeLists.txt:14-20 runs git rev-parse, whose empty output shadows the cache value, unless GIT_EXE is off (boltbeam-runs/decode-topk-fused-20261115 Round 2, measured 2026-11-16)
llama.cpp.offline_cmake_why: a mods build is a copy of a tree already on the machine and needs no network: with the option on (the engine's default, CMakeLists.txt:138) the build step tries to fetch llama-server's page assets from a remote bucket (scripts/ui-assets.cmake); without network that fetch fails after its timeout and what gets embedded then depends on the network. BoltBeam drives llama-server through its API only. A stock install (data/engine_releases.json) keeps the engine's default, so a stock and a mods build of one base may differ in the embedded page, nothing else. Measured: the b12521 mods tree of boltbeam-runs/gdn-gate-live-20261119 was configured with it and the commit flags above (its README, Process: Tree), embedded 0 assets and loaded its region manifest

commit_header.why: the commit ggml_commit() returns, the one the ext-kernels hook compares with a manifest's engine.builds

own_patches_why: the arkey capture patch belongs to arkey, BoltBeam's own provider and search machinery, not a target inference engine: it stays in tools/patches

evidence_patches.why: evidence records: the files the 2026-10-27 R9700 runs applied, kept verbatim beside their sources.md; the mods themselves live in arkey_ie_mods; the amd-r9700-patches-20261114 three are the R9700 box's 2026-11-14 llama.cpp patches (an AVX-512 IQ2_XXS dot product, GGML_SCHED_BATCH_GETS, GGML_CUDA_SYNC_SPIN), parked here until they are ported to arkey_ie_mods as mods
